shots.title: Which routes reach the marked spot?
shots.caption: Write a route with {moves} moves. At each step, choose right or up.

shots.title: Each choice opens another branch.
shots.caption: Each leaf is a possible route. One more move doubles the number of possibilities.

shots.title: What do the first trials establish?
shots.caption: Try {budget} routes. Of those, {trialHits} reach the goal. The other {untested} routes are still untested.

shots.title: Look at where the paths meet.
shots.caption: The order of the moves does not change the endpoint. Each number counts the routes that meet there.

shots.title: Which correct route would you keep?
shots.caption: All {solutions} routes reach the same square. Count their turns and {optima} tie for the minimum.

shots.title: What can the language express?
shots.caption: A right-only language can reach only the bottom row. Adding “up” makes a solution expressible.

shots.title: In program synthesis, each candidate is a program.
shots.caption: Test each program on every byte. Only the interval with both boundaries in the right places survives.

shots.title: Carry the discovery to a new problem.
shots.caption: On an open grid, the move counts determine the endpoint. Use them to build a route directly.

shots.title: Every well-defined problem can be modeled as search.
shots.caption: The problem tells us which answers count. A good method discovers how much search we can avoid.
